capabilities: read notes aloud as chapters split by headings, with a floating player
cache chapter recordings and re-record only chapters you edited
speak with an offline natural voice, the system voice, OpenAI, Google Gemini, or your own server
translate non-English notes to English before reading
export a note as a single MP3 file
extras: Desktop only (Windows, macOS, Linux). Licensed under GNU AGPL v3.0. The manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The built-in natural voice and translation models are free and offline; OpenAI and Gemini voices bill your account.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to listen to a note read aloud, so users must copy text into other TTS tools or lose their place when re-reading edited notes.

relations.evidence: The idea of reading Obsidian notes aloud with a floating player came from Obsidian Edge TTS
For OpenAI itself choose Quick setup → OpenAI and add your API key.
Create an API key in Google AI Studio.

summary: Text-to-speech player that reads notes aloud like an audiobook, splitting them into chapters by heading, with an offline natural voice and MP3 export.
